title: Scaling Laws and Tradeoffs in Recurrent Networks of Expressive Neurons
abstract: arXiv:2605.12049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cortical neurons are complex, multi-timescale processors wired into recurrent circuits, shaped by long evolutionary pressure under stringent biological constraints. Mainstream machine learning, by contrast, predominantly builds models from extremely simple units, a default inherited from early neural-network theory. We treat this as a normative architectural question. How should one split a fixed parameter budget $P$ between the number of units $N$, per-unit effective complexity $k_e$, and per-unit connectivity $k_c$? What controls the optimal allocation? This calls for a model in which per-unit complexity can be tuned independently of width and connectivity. Accordingly, we introduce the ELM Network, whose recurrent layer is built from Expressive Leaky Memory (ELM) neurons, chosen to mirror functional components of cortical neurons. translated_title: 表达性神经元循环网络中的缩放定律与权衡
translated_abstract: 皮层神经元是复杂的、具有多时间尺度的处理器，它们连接成循环回路，是在严格的生物约束下经长期进化压力塑造而成的。相比之下，主流机器学习主要由极其简单的单元构建模型，这是从早期神经网络理论继承下来的默认做法。我们将此视为一个规范性的架构问题：应如何在单元数量 $N$、单元有效复杂度 $k_e$ 和单元连接度 $k_c$ 之间分配固定的参数预算 $P$？是什么因素控制着最优分配？这需要一个能够独立于宽度和连接度来调节单元复杂度的模型。为此，我们引入了 ELM 网络，其循环层由“表达性泄漏记忆”神经元构成，该神经元的设计模拟了皮层神经元的功能组件。该架构允许对 $N$、$k_e$ 和 $k_c$ 进行单独调节，并能稳定地进行训练。
tldr: 该论文提出由表达性泄漏记忆（ELM）神经元构成的循环网络，研究在固定参数预算下如何在神经元数量、单元复杂度与连接度之间进行最优分配的缩放定律与权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the ELM Network, built from Expressive Leaky Memory neurons, to study scaling laws and tradeoffs in optimally allocating a fixed parameter budget across unit count, per-unit complexity, and connectivity.
